title: Design decisions: broadcast-scope mention wire format and semantics
description:
Make the design decisions for broadcast-scope @-mentions BEFORE any spec edits. Each decision below has two-or-more coherent answers; this bead exists to choose, document, and unblock the implementation beads.

This bead is BLOCKING for jmap-chat-spec-fig9.2 (main draft implementation) and indirectly for the other Epic A children.

---

DECISION 1 — Wire format / type discriminator location

Path A — Extend the Mention type at draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md:263 with a `type` field:
  Mention {
    type: "user" | "everyone" | "here" | "admins",
    id: String (optional, present when type=="user"),
    offset: UnsignedInt,
    length: UnsignedInt
  }

Path B — Keep the Mention type per-user only; add a separate `broadcastMentions` array on Message with its own structure.

Recommendation: Path A. Cleaner; one structure handles both.

---

DECISION 2 — Rich-body span treatment

The `"mention"` span in the rich-body model (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md:1285) carries `userId`. Either:
- Add new span types per scope: `"mention-everyone"`, `"mention-here"`, `"mention-admins"`
- Extend the existing `"mention"` span with a `scope` field: `"user" | "everyone" | "here" | "admins"`, with `userId` conditional on `scope: "user"`

Recommendation: extend existing.

---

DECISION 3 — Permission model

The `mention_all` permission at draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md:582 currently gates Space-wide @mentions. Options:
- Umbrella: `mention_all` covers all three broadcast scopes
- Per-scope permissions: `mention_everyone`, `mention_here`, `mention_admins` as separate permissions in the closed vocabulary

Recommendation: umbrella. Simpler vocabulary, less wire surface. But this is a real choice — granular permissioning is a legitimate ask in some deployments.

---

DECISION 4 — Receiver-side recipient resolution

For routing/push/UX purposes, which members are "targeted" by each broadcast scope:
- `@everyone`: all current members (deterministic)
- `@here`: members with active presence. Server-defined exactly which presence state (`"online"`? `"online" | "away"`?). When is the set computed (send-time on sender's server, or delivery-time on each receiving server)?
- `@admins`: members holding administrative permissions. Server-defined which permissions count (`manage_space`? any `manage_*`? controller principals from §Space Governance?). When is the set computed?

Recommendation: send-time set is informational; delivery-time set on the receiving server is authoritative for push urgency and badging.

---

DECISION 5 — Suppression preferences

The spec already has `Chat.muted`, `Chat.receiveTypingIndicators`, `Chat.receiptSharing`, and `Chat.muteUntil`. Adding broadcast mentions raises:
- Can a member opt out of `@here` notifications while still receiving `@everyone`?
- Can a member opt out of `@everyone` ever, or is it always elevated (forced unmute)?
- What about `@admins` if you are an admin?
- Does `Chat.muted: true` suppress broadcast mentions, or are they an exception?

This is the rabbit hole. Many existing systems (notably Slack with `@channel`) handle this poorly. The decision here directly informs which preference fields appear in Chat-update payloads.

Recommendation: NEEDS DISCUSSION. Conservative default: broadcast mentions bypass `Chat.muted` for the targeted recipients but are otherwise filtered by existing preferences; per-scope opt-out preferences are a future bead. But this needs explicit alignment before locking in.

---

DECISION 6 — Push payload representation

The push draft has `hasMention` and `hasMentionAll` boolean fields (lines 177-180). Options:
- Keep these two; `hasMentionAll` becomes true for any broadcast scope. Loses fidelity.
- Add per-scope flags: `hasMentionEveryone`, `hasMentionHere`, `hasMentionAdmins`. Verbose.
- Replace with a typed field: `mentionScopes: ["user" | "everyone" | "here" | "admins"]`. Cleaner.

Recommendation: replace with a typed field. But this is a wire-format change to the push draft and warrants its own thought.

---

Open questions to resolve in this bead:
- Confirm or override each recommendation above
- Whether to ship all three broadcast scopes at once or stage them (`@everyone` first, `@here` and `@admins` follow)
- Whether the design accommodates future scopes (e.g., `@channel-managers`, `@bots`) cleanly
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of the six decisions has a documented chosen answer (yes/no/which-option)
- The suppression-preferences decision in particular has explicit alignment, not a default
- An updated dependency graph or comment explains which downstream beads are unblocked
- The chosen wire format is unambiguous enough that jmap-chat-spec-fig9.2 (main draft implementation) can begin without further design discussion
close_reason: All eight decisions made in collaborative session 2026-05-12. Decision record in comments unblocks fig9.2, fig9.3, fig9.4. See comment for D1-D6 + M1 + M2 resolutions.
